source.table: HEV-5 / HEV-RN-5 / HSM-5; PH STAINLESS STEEL: 15-5, 17-4, Carpenter 450, Carpenter 465; Hardness 21 - 36 HRC
source.cells: SFM 200; IPT .0002 (Slot column under 1/16); ADOC 30%-75% Diameter; RDOC 100% Diameter

vendor_notes: Hardness Scales: HRB = Rockwell B; HRC = Rockwell C
IPT values shown are for 2.5xD length of cut tools, and should be adjusted for longer or shorter lengths of cut.
Values shown are for non-reached tools. For tools with reaches greater than 3xD, IPT should be reduced.
For more accurate running parameters, please refer to Machining Advisor Pro.
rows.notes: Row hardness 21-36 HRC straddles the sheet's 35 HRC split in the ADOC/RDOC table; the "< 35 HRC" DOC rows were applied. Tool picked from the vendor product page as the stocked square, non-Weldon part with LOC closest to 2.5xD (the length the IPT is stated for); ties go to shorter LOC. Chart covers the whole series so this is one valid representative. variable_pitch=true taken from the product title "Variable Pitch"; helix angle is not printed on the product page. Chart row alignment (material label to hardness rows) read from the rendered page; row values from pdftotext -raw. ADOC numeric value: range 0.01875-0.04688 in; ap uses the midpoint/limit shown.

source.table: HEM Tooling - 1/2" 5-Flute End Mill in 17-4ph (36 Rc) - (HEV-5)
source.cells: 1/2" 5-Flute End Mill in 17-4ph (36 Rc) - (HEV-5): HEM RPM 6,000; IPM 80; RDOC .062 (12%); ADOC .500 (100%); MRR 2.50

vendor_notes: The following case studies illustrate the power of HEM using Helical end mills versus traditional roughing (page intro).
High Efficiency RDOC Strategy: Lowered RDOC = 7%-30% x D; Increased IPM = chip thinning parameter must include 'inside arc' feed reduction; Utilize HE type of tool paths for best results (p.31).
High Efficiency ADOC Strategy: Up to 2 x dia. ADOC; utilizes majority of LOC (p.32).
rows.notes: Shop case study, not a chart recommendation: a single published cut with its outcome (cycle time, parts per tool). SFM and fz computed from the printed RPM/IPM: SFM = 6000 x pi x 0.5 / 12 = 785.4; fz = 80 / (6000 x 5) = 0.002667 in. Printed MRR 2.50 in^3/min = IPM x RDOC x ADOC checks out (2.48). The guidebook names only the series and diameter, not a part number, LOC, shank or coating, so those are null. Values read from pdftotext -layout and checked against the rendered p.25. Outcome printed: cycle time per part 7:00, 40 parts per tool (vs 15 traditional). The 785 SFM is far above the HEV-5 chart's 145-200 SFM for PH stainless (21-50 HRC); the calibration step should treat this row as one shop result, not a vendor envelope.
